storySpine.startingBelief: B.Com is purely for accounting and excludes business management.
storySpine.studentSituation: Student is applying to BBA programs only, believing B.Com is too narrow for their management goals.
storySpine.observation: Scanning the JOY University 2025-26 curriculum documents, they see 'Business Organization & Management' listed in both B.Com (p.5) and BBA (p.9) Semester I.
storySpine.focus: The assumption that degree titles act as perfect partitions for subject matter.
storySpine.whyQuestionFollows: If the same foundational course appears in both, the title alone does not define the full curriculum breadth.
storySpine.changedAction: The student adds B.Com to their provisional research list.
storySpine.visibleConsequence: They stop filtering B.Com out and begin comparing specific subject lists rather than relying on degree labels.
storySpine.channelExperience: The audience sees the direct evidence of a shared course title, shifting their perspective from title-based exclusion to module-based investigation.

selected.title: Beyond the Degree Title
selected.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles dictate subject exclusivity.
selected.hlni: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of the published JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents whose covers say students admitted from 2025–26 onwards.
selected.viewerChange: Viewers will evaluate courses by specific modules rather than rejecting them based on labels.
selected.support: Official JOY University PDF, B.Com Accounting & Finance p.5 and BBA Entrepreneurship Management p.9; covers identify the 2025–26-onwards cohort.
methodSteps: Identify the specific programme and document cohort.
Show the inspected course-title row in each source.
Use this bounded overlap to investigate the full course, rather than assume degree titles partition subjects.
selected.interpretationRule: The supplied rows establish this shared title in these two documents only; they do not establish identical teaching, depth, assessment or availability.
selected.visibleProof: Two real cited rows correct a title-based assumption while retaining programme/version scope.
selected.payoff: A more inclusive and evidence-based shortlist for academic planning.
selected.limitations: No universal overlap, identical content, exclusivity, current-admissions or career inference. BBA later sections are inconsistent; use only the inspected row.

demonstration.observation: Both B.Com and BBA programmes include this exact course.
demonstration.nextQuestion: What other modules define the actual depth of these programs?

conceptSelection.contrast: Only Trust was planned and reviewed. Finished-story channel comparison is separate; this is not editorial approval.

hlni.insight: Business Organization & Management is listed in Semester I of both the JOY University B.Com Accounting & Finance and BBA Entrepreneurship Management documents for 2025-26 entrants.
hlni.audienceGap: Students assume degree titles mean subjects are entirely different or exclusive.
hlni.viewerChange: Viewers will stop filtering programs by title alone and start comparing specific module lists.
hlni.support: Official JOY University programme documents for B.Com Accounting & Finance (p.5) and BBA Entrepreneurship Management (p.9), 2025–26 cohort.
hlni.payoff: The student realizes the title is not a definitive filter and decides to compare full module lists, leading to a broader, evidence-based shortlist.

objective: Help students move from label-based degree selection to module-based investigation.
targetAudience: +2 students seeking academic depth and well-supported course and career decisions

shots.name: The Title Assumption
shots.visual: A student holds two printed program flyers, B.Com and BBA, looking frustrated.
shots.dialogue: I thought B.Com was only for accounting.

shots.name: The Narrow Research
shots.visual: Student scribbles a giant 'X' over the B.Com flyer.
shots.cameraPerformance: Focus on the pen hitting the paper.

shots.name: The Evidence Reveal
shots.visual: Student places two official curriculum PDFs side-by-side, pointing to a highlighted row.
shots.dialogue: Look at Semester I in both documents.
shots.cameraPerformance: Top-down view of the desk surface.

shots.name: The Overlap Insight
shots.visual: Student looks between the two documents in surprise.
shots.dialogue: Foundational management is in both. Titles aren't fixed partitions.
shots.cameraPerformance: Reaction shot, looking into the camera.

shots.name: The Shift in Strategy
shots.visual: Student removes the 'X' from the B.Com flyer and starts listing other modules to compare.
shots.dialogue: What other modules define the actual depth of these programs?
shots.cameraPerformance: Tracking shot showing the student comparing lists.

shots.name: The Research Action
shots.visual: Student neatly aligns both flyers side-by-side on the desk.
shots.dialogue: Check official documents before you decide.
shots.cameraPerformance: Final wide shot of the organized desk.

productionNotes.visualStyle: Clean, academic desk setting with clear document overlays.
productionNotes.camera: Handheld for intimacy, static for document clarity.
productionNotes.editing: Direct cuts to match the reveal of evidence.
productionNotes.sound: Minimal ambient room sound, clear voiceover.

creativeSummary.keyCreativeIdea: Use a verified shared course title to break the assumption that degree titles act as absolute partitions, shifting the student toward evidence-based investigation.
